theme: I will call on the name of the LORD
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 116. Romans 10:13 says that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. This psalm is a testimony of someone who did exactly that. Notice the movement from near-death to thanksgiving.
settingTheScene: Psalm 116 is a song of thanksgiving by someone who has been rescued from death. It is part of the Hallel (Psalms 113 to 118) that Jews sang at Passover. On the night before he was crucified, Jesus and his disciples would have sung these psalms after the supper (Matthew 26:30). So these words were in the air in the upper room. The phrase “call on the name of the LORD” appears four times and links to Romans 10.
observation: “I love the LORD, because he has heard my voice and my pleas for mercy” (v. 1).
“The snares of death encompassed me; the pangs of Sheol laid hold on me; I suffered distress and anguish” (v. 3).
“Then I called on the name of the LORD: O LORD, I pray, deliver my soul!” (v. 4).
“Gracious is the LORD, and righteous; our God is merciful” (v. 5).
“For you have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from stumbling” (v. 8).
“What shall I render to the LORD for all his benefits to me?” (v. 12).
“I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the LORD” (v. 13).
“Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints” (v. 15).
interpretation:
The psalm starts with love: “I love the LORD, because he has heard my voice.” Gratitude for answered prayer produces love. Because God inclined his ear, the psalmist says, “I will call on him as long as I live.” It is a lifelong promise.

Then he tells the story. The snares of death surrounded him, the pangs of Sheol laid hold of him. We do not know the illness or danger, but it was severe. “Then I called on the name of the LORD: O LORD, I pray, deliver my soul!” It is a short prayer, the prayer of someone with no time for long speeches. And God answered. Notice what the psalmist says about God’s character: gracious, righteous, merciful, one who preserves the simple. “When I was brought low, he saved me.” The simple are not fools but those who depend on God rather than on their own cleverness.

The psalmist addresses his own soul: “Return, O my soul, to your rest, for the LORD has dealt bountifully with you.” Rest follows rescue. He has been delivered from death, tears, and stumbling, and he resolves to walk before the LORD in the land of the living.

Then the question that fits all Christians: “What shall I render to the LORD for all his benefits to me?” How can we repay God? We can’t. The answer is surprising: “I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the LORD.” The way to respond to a gift is to receive it again, gladly. The cup of salvation recalls the cup of the Passover. For Christians, it recalls the cup that Jesus gave his disciples, the new covenant in his blood. We do not repay God; we take the cup and thank him.

Verse 15 says, “Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints.” For the believer, death is not meaningless. God notices and values the death of each one who belongs to him. The psalmist is also a servant, the son of God’s maidservant, whose chains the LORD has loosed. He promises to pay his vows in the presence of all the people, in the courts of the house of the LORD. Thanksgiving is public.

This is a good psalm to pray after a hard season. And when we read it as Jesus’ hymn, we see that on the night he was betrayed he sang of the cup of salvation, then went out to drink the cup of suffering. The LORD would deliver his soul from death, not by sparing him but by raising him.
connection: Romans 10:13 and Joel 2:32 speak of calling on the name of the LORD. Psalm 113 to 118 are the Hallel. Matthew 26:27-30 and Luke 22:17-20 describe the cup and the hymn. 1 Corinthians 10:16 and 11:25 speak of the cup of blessing. Psalm 56:12-13 also gives thanks for deliverance. Psalm 91 speaks of refuge and rescue. Philippians 1:21-23 speaks of death as gain. Hebrews 5:7 says Jesus offered up prayers with loud cries to him who was able to save him from death. Revelation 14:13 says blessed are the dead who die in the Lord.
application:
Pray the short prayer of verse 4 for a situation today: O LORD, I pray, deliver my soul.

Ask what you will render to the LORD for his benefits. Take the cup of salvation by thanking him aloud for specific gifts.

Next time you take the Lord’s Supper, remember that Jesus sang this psalm.
prayerPrompts: Tell God you love him because he hears.
Thank him for saving you from death.
Ask him what you can render for all his benefits.
